extracted.name: Almond Cake
extracted.description: This recipe published by Amanda Hesser is for almond lovers like me. It's not the prettiest cake in the world because it crumbles on the edges and falls in the middle, but it is flawless otherwise. If you care about looks, dust it with confectioners' sugar just before serving.
ingredient_lines: 226 grams (2 sticks) butter, softened between 65F and 68F (149C to 154C), more for buttering pan
240 grams (2 cups) all-purpose flour (or 190 grams + 50 grams almond meal)
220 grams (or 1 cup plus 2 tablespoons) granulated sugar
236 grams (1 cup) sour cream or Greek yogurt
Confectioners’ sugar, for sifting over cake
instruction_lines: Preheat oven to 325 degrees. Butter sides and bottom of a 10-inch pan (or 2 8-inch cake or springform pans) and line bottom with parchment paper. Butter paper. Place pan in freezer.

Sift flour and salt into a small bowl. Set aside. In a mixer fitted with a paddle, beat butter and granulated sugar at medium speed until fluffy, about 5 minutes. Add almond paste, a little at a time at medium speed, and beat 8 minutes.
Beat in egg yolks, one at a time, and almond extract. Mix sour cream and baking soda and add to butter mixture. Reduce mixer speed to low and gradually add flour mixture, just until blended.

Put batter in prepared pan and spread evenly. Sprinkle sliced almonds, if desired. Bake about 40 minutes, until top is golden and spring back when lightly pressed and cake shrinks from sides of the pan. Cool in pan on wire rack. Remove sides of pan and remove paper.
When ready to serve, sift confectioners’ sugar on top and slice like pie.
